aaron.title: Aaron
aaron.about: High Priest living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
aaron.note: Moses's older brother, and the one God sent to do the talking when Moses said he could not. He became Israel's first high priest, and the priesthood ran through his sons after him. Most of the time he is standing next to Moses.

abdon-3.title: Abdon
abdon-3.note: One of the minor judges, son of Hillel. What got written down about him is the size of his family, sons and grandsons enough that all of them riding donkeys was worth recording, and eight years judging Israel.

abel-meholah.title: Abel-meholah
abel-meholah.note: A town in the Jordan Valley on the road the Midianites took when they ran from Gideon. It is also where Elisha came from: Elijah found him there behind a plough.

abiezer-2.title: Abiezer
abiezer-2.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
abiezer-2.note: The man Gideon's clan is named after, in Manasseh. Gideon's own description of that clan, when he was called, was the weakest in the tribe.

abiezrite.title: Abiezrite
abiezrite.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
abiezrite.note: The name for anyone out of that clan, based at Ophrah. Gideon called it the weakest family in his tribe, and that is where the man who broke Midian's grip on Israel came from.

abimelech.title: Abimelech
abimelech.note: Gideon's son by a concubine. He killed almost all seventy of his brothers to clear his own way, which is most of what Judges has to say about him.

abinoam.title: Abinoam
abinoam.note: Barak's father, and that is the whole of it. Barak is the commander Deborah sent for when Israel went up against Sisera.

accho.title: Accho
accho.note: A Phoenician port on the coast north of Mount Carmel. It was handed to Asher, and Asher never took it.

achsah.title: Achsah
achsah.note: Caleb's daughter, married to Othniel after he took a Canaanite city. She asked her father for springs of water, and got them.

achzib-2.title: Achzib
achzib-2.note: The other Achzib, a Phoenician town on the coast inside Asher's territory that Israel never fully took.

adonibezek.title: Adonibezek
adonibezek.note: He ruled at Bezek, a Canaanite king who had beaten seventy rival chiefs, cut off their thumbs and big toes, and left them to scavenge scraps under his table. The tribes of Judah and Simeon defeated him.

ahiman.title: Ahiman
ahiman.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
ahiman.note: One of the descendants of Anak. That clan's size terrified the Israelite spies. Decades later Caleb drove Ahiman and his brothers out of Hebron, the land he had been promised.

ahlab.title: Ahlab
ahlab.note: Asher was given this Phoenician town and never took it, so its Canaanite inhabitants went on living there beside the Israelites. It is generally identified with Khirbet el-Mahalib on the Lebanese coast, a few miles north of Tyre.

aijalon.title: Aijalon
aijalon.note: In the valley of Aijalon Joshua told the moon to stand still alongside the sun during the battle against the Amorite coalition. Later it marked the boundary of Danite and Benjamite territory.

amalek.title: Amalek
amalek.note: Esau's grandson. The Amalekites who came from him attacked the weak rear of Israel's column in the wilderness, and God declared war on Amalek for it. Saul's half-done obedience against them later cost him the kingdom.

ammon.title: Ammon
ammon.note: A nation east of the Jordan, descended from Lot through his younger daughter and close kin to Moab. The Ammonites fought Israel again and again, from Jephthah's war in Judges to the insult to David's envoys that started a full war in David's reign.

amorite.title: Amorite
amorite.note: One of the peoples in Canaan before Israel came, traced in Genesis 10 to a son of Canaan, and sometimes used loosely for everyone in the hill country. Sihon and Og ruled an Amorite kingdom east of the Jordan that fell to Israel under Moses. Outside the Bible they are the Amurru of Mesopotamian texts, the people whose dynasty produced Hammurabi of Babylon.

anakim.title: Anakim
anakim.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
anakim.note: A people of unusual height living in Canaan before the conquest. Ten of the twelve spies came back afraid of them, and that fear is why Israel spent forty years in the wilderness.

anath.title: Anath
anath.note: Shamgar's father. Shamgar killed six hundred Philistines with an ox goad. The name matches the Canaanite goddess Anat, but here it is just what his father was called.

aphek-2.title: Aphek
aphek-2.note: Two battles happened here. The Philistines took the ark from Israel at Aphek, and later Israel beat the Arameans here, exactly as Elisha had said.

arad.title: Arad
arad.note: Its king attacked Israel as they came up toward Canaan from the south and took prisoners, and Israel destroyed the town under the ban. The Canaanite city lay about 20 miles south of Hebron, at Tel Arad.

aram.title: Aram
aram.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
aram.note: It is what the Old Testament calls Syria, the region and people centred on Damascus. Under kings like Ben-hadad and Hazael it fought both Israelite kingdoms again and again.

aram-naharaim.title: Aram-naharaim
aram-naharaim.note: Aram of the two rivers, upper Mesopotamia. Abraham's relatives settled there, and the wives of Isaac and Jacob came from it.

arnon.title: Arnon
arnon.note: A swift river running into the Dead Sea from the east, the line between Amorite and later Moabite land and Israel's tribes beyond the Jordan. Its gorge still carries water in the Wadi al-Mujib. King Mesha of Moab's inscription, the Moabite Stone, boasts of building a highway across it.

aroer.title: Aroer
aroer.note: A border town on the edge of Moabite and Ammonite territory. It marked the southern limit of the land Israel took east of the Jordan.

aroer-2.title: Aroer
aroer-2.note: A second town of the name, in Numbers 32:34 and Joshua 13:25, on the same border between Israel's lands east of the Jordan and Ammonite territory.

asher.title: Asher
asher.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
asher.note: Jacob's eighth son, by Leah's servant Zilpah. His tribe got a fertile coastal strip in the north, running toward Phoenicia, some of the richest land in Israel. Beyond its borders and city list little of the tribe's own history is recorded, and like Simeon it produced no judge or great hero.

asherites.title: Asherites
asherites.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
asherites.note: The tribe of Asher. Judges 1:32 says they never drove out the Canaanites of their coastal land and settled down among them instead.

ashkelon.title: Ashkelon
ashkelon.note: One of the five main Philistine cities, a port on the coast midway between Gaza and Joppa. Samson killed thirty of its men there to pay off a wager. It is named on the Merneptah Stele, an Egyptian inscription from around 1208 BC.

ashtoreth.title: Ashtoreth
ashtoreth.about: A female deity in the Old Testament
ashtoreth.note: A Canaanite and Phoenician goddess of fertility and war, closely tied to Baal worship. Solomon built her a shrine late in his reign to please a foreign wife, and that is given as a main reason the kingdom split.

azzah.title: Azzah
azzah.note: Gaza, under a more literal spelling. The southernmost of the five chief Philistine cities, it sat on the coastal road between Egypt and Canaan.

baal.title: Baal
baal.about: A male deity in the Old Testament
baal.note: The Canaanite storm god, the power people believed sent the rain and made the crops grow. Worshipping him was the temptation Israel never shook, and the Old Testament fights it from the judges onward.

baal-berith.title: Baal-berith
baal-berith.about: A male deity in the Old Testament
baal-berith.note: Lord of the covenant. Israel went after this Canaanite god at Shechem once Gideon was dead, and his shrine there comes up again in the next chapter.

baal-hermon.title: Baal-hermon
baal-hermon.note: Two things carry the name. One is a town near Mount Hermon where the half-tribe of Manasseh lived, maybe the same place as Baal-gad. The other is the mountain itself, on the list of Canaanite strongholds.

baal-tamar.title: Baal-tamar
baal-tamar.note: Lord of the palm tree. It sat near Gibeah in Benjamin. The other tribes regrouped there for their final assault on Benjamin, in the civil war the outrage at Gibeah set off.

balak.title: Balak
balak.about: King living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
balak.note: The Moabite king who paid Balaam to curse Israel and got blessings instead, oracle after oracle. His temper fraying each time is one of the darkly comic threads in Numbers.

barak.title: Barak
barak.note: He led Israel against Sisera, the Canaanite general, because Deborah told him to, and he would not go unless she came with him. That hesitation cost him the glory of the win.

beer-shebah.title: Beer-shebah
beer-shebah.note: From Dan to Beersheba meant all of Israel, top to bottom, and this was the bottom. It marked the southern edge of Judah's land and went first to Simeon. Genesis gives two separate stories for how it got its name.

beeroth-2.title: Beeroth
beeroth-2.note: Named once, in Judges, and nowhere else.

benjamin.title: Benjamin
benjamin.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
benjamin.note: Jacob's twelfth son and the youngest, born to Rachel on the road near Bethlehem as she died giving birth to him. Jacob guarded him fiercely after losing Joseph. That fear drives much of the tension in Joseph's story.

berith.title: Berith
berith.about: A male deity in the Old Testament
berith.note: Covenant. This Berith is a Canaanite god worshipped at Shechem, and the house of El-berith was his temple stronghold, where the people of Shechem took refuge from Abimelech.

beth-anath.title: Beth-anath
beth-anath.note: House of Anath, named for the Canaanite goddess. Naphtali was given this fortified town. They never drove out the Canaanites in it and put them to forced labor instead.

beth-barah.title: Beth-barah
beth-barah.note: House of the crossing, a ford of the Jordan. Gideon sent word ahead to seize it before the fleeing Midianites got there, and the men of Ephraim caught and killed the Midianite commanders.

beth-el.title: Beth-el
beth-el.note: About ten miles north of Jerusalem, and once the Canaanite city of Luz. Abram built an altar there. Jacob dreamed of a ladder reaching to heaven there and called the place house of God.

beth-rehob.title: Beth-rehob
beth-rehob.note: A small Aramean kingdom in the north, near the valley where the Danites took Laish and renamed it Dan. It also sent mercenaries to the Ammonites.

beth-shean.title: Beth-shean
beth-shean.note: After Saul died on Gilboa, the Philistines hung his body and his sons' bodies on the walls of this city. Beth-shean was Canaanite, in Manasseh's land. It stood where the Jezreel and Jordan valleys meet.

beth-shemesh-2.title: Beth-shemesh
beth-shemesh-2.note: Named twice, in Joshua and Judges, and nowhere else.

beth-shittah.title: Beth-shittah
beth-shittah.note: House of the acacia. The Midianite army fled toward it after Gideon's night attack broke their camp, somewhere in the Jordan valley near Beth-shean.

bethlehem.title: Bethlehem
bethlehem.note: House of bread. It is a small town about five miles south of Jerusalem, earlier called Ephrath, where Rachel died and was buried and where Ruth gleaned in Boaz's fields. David was born there and anointed there.

bezek.title: Bezek
bezek.note: Judah and Simeon beat the Canaanite king Adoni-bezek here, near Jerusalem, and cut off his thumbs and big toes. He admitted he had done the same to other kings.

bochim.title: Bochim
bochim.note: Here the angel of the Lord confronted Israel for making treaties with the Canaanites. The people wept bitterly, and the weeping gave the place its name. Nobody has identified the site, though it was likely near Bethel or Shiloh.

cain.title: Cain
cain.about: Man living at the time before the Flood
cain.note: Adam and Eve's firstborn, a farmer. God accepted his brother Abel's offering and not his, and Cain killed Abel out of jealousy. God marked him and sent him off to wander rather than putting him to death.

caleb.title: Caleb
caleb.about: Joshua's compatriot living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness and Conquest
caleb.note: One of the twelve spies Moses sent into Canaan. He and Joshua were the only two who came back telling Israel to trust God and take the land, and the rest of that generation paid for ignoring them with forty years in the wilderness.

camon.title: Camon
camon.note: Jair was buried here, the judge who led Israel for twenty-two years. Where it was is disputed: tradition puts it in Gilead east of the Jordan, or else near Mount Carmel.

canaan.title: Canaan
canaan.note: The land promised to Abraham and his descendants, roughly modern Israel and the land around it. The conquest under Joshua is that promise, centuries old by then, being kept.

canaanite.title: Canaanite
canaanite.note: They were the people living in the land promised to Israel. The biblical genealogy traces them to Canaan, son of Ham. The Old Testament repeatedly orders them driven out because of their idol worship and other practices.

chemosh.title: Chemosh
chemosh.about: A male deity in the Old Testament
chemosh.note: Moab's national god. Solomon built him a shrine to please one of his foreign wives, and that is among the reasons given for the enemies God raised against Solomon late in his reign.

chushan-rishathayim.title: Chushan-rishathayim
chushan-rishathayim.note: God let this king of Aram-naharaim hold Israel down for eight years, the first foreign oppression in Judges. Othniel, Caleb's younger kinsman, beat him, and the land had forty years of peace. The name means something like doubly wicked Cushan, which may be a Hebrew jab rather than what he was really called.

dagon.title: Dagon
dagon.about: A male deity in the Old Testament
dagon.note: The Philistines set the captured ark in Dagon's temple at Ashdod. His statue was found face down before the ark, and the second time it had lost its head and hands.

dan.title: Dan
dan.note: The tribe of Dan and the town it took. Squeezed in its first allotment near the Philistines, the tribe went north, captured Laish and renamed it Dan, Israel's northernmost town and the far end of from Dan to Beersheba. Jeroboam I put one of his golden calves there, and a stele from Tel Dan found in 1993 names the House of David.

debir.title: Debir
debir.note: Othniel took this town in Judah's hill country and won Caleb's daughter Achsah as his wife for it. Debir is also the name of a Canaanite king Joshua defeated.

deborah.title: Deborah
deborah.note: Prophetess and the one woman among Israel's judges. She sat under a palm tree between Ramah and Bethel and Israel came to her for judgment. Barak would not go against Sisera without her, so she went and told him a woman would get the credit, and Jael killed Sisera in her own tent.

delilah.title: Delilah
delilah.note: Samson loved her, and the Philistine rulers paid her well to find out where his strength came from. He lied three times and each answer failed. She kept at him until he told her about his uncut Nazirite hair, and she had it shaved while he slept.

dodo-3.title: Dodo
dodo-3.note: One of 3 men called Dodo. This one is a man from the years before the monarchy, named once in Judges.

dor.title: Dor
dor.note: A royal Canaanite port on the coast south of Mount Carmel. Joshua beat its king, but its people were never fully driven out, and it later went into one of Solomon's districts. Excavation at Tel Dor traces the shift from Canaanite to Phoenician on that coast.

ebed.title: Ebed
ebed.note: Father of Gaal, the man who stirred Shechem up against Abimelech.

edom.title: Edom
edom.note: Esau got the byname Edom over a bowl of red stew, and it stuck to the mountain country his descendants settled southeast of the Dead Sea. Bozrah was its old capital and Sela, the Greeks' Petra, its rock fortress. Edom refused Israel passage in the exodus and later helped Babylon sack Jerusalem, and the prophets did not let that go.

eglon-2.title: Eglon
eglon-2.note: King of Moab. With Ammon and Amalek he took Jericho and held Israel down for eighteen years, until Ehud, the left-handed judge, killed him.

egypt.title: Egypt
egypt.note: Joseph rose to power there and kept his family alive through the famine. A later pharaoh enslaved their descendants, and that set up the exodus. For the rest of the Old Testament Egypt stands for the slavery Israel was brought out of, and Matthew has Jesus's family flee there from Herod as if living that story again.

ehud.title: Ehud
ehud.note: A left-handed judge from the tribe of Benjamin. He strapped a dagger to his right thigh, where nobody checks a right-handed man, killed the fat Moabite king Eglon, and locked the doors behind him on the way out. Israel then routed the Moabites and had eighty years of rest, the longest in Judges.

ekron.title: Ekron
ekron.note: Northernmost of the five Philistine cities, given to Judah and then Dan but never firmly held. The ark's last stop before the Philistines sent it back. Ahaziah of Israel sent there to ask Baal-zebub about his health, and an inscription at Tel Miqne naming Ikausu, or Achish, son of Padi settles the site.

eleazar.title: Eleazar
eleazar.about: High Priest living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
eleazar.note: Aaron's third son. Nadab and Abihu died for offering unauthorized fire, and Eleazar became high priest after his father. He worked with Moses on the second census and with Joshua on dividing the land, and his line held the high priesthood for most of the history after.

elon-3.title: Elon
elon-3.note: Hebrew for oak, which is why it lands on a town and on several men. This one is in the family lists.

en-hakhore.title: En-hakhore
en-hakhore.note: Spring of the one who called, the water God opened at Lehi for Samson after the jawbone fight.

ephraim.title: Ephraim
ephraim.about: Joseph's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
ephraim.note: Joseph's younger son. When Jacob blessed the two boys he crossed his hands on purpose and gave Ephraim the bigger blessing over Manasseh. The tribe came to dominate the north so much that the prophets use Ephraim for the whole northern kingdom.

ephraimite.title: Ephraimite
ephraimite.about: Joseph's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
ephraimite.note: Someone of the tribe of Ephraim. In Judges 12 the men of Gilead caught Ephraimites at the fords by making them say shibboleth, and killed those who could not get the first sound right.

eshtaol.title: Eshtaol
eshtaol.note: Samson grew up here, and here the Spirit of the Lord first began to stir him. It was a Shephelah town that went to Dan, and the Danites sent their spies north from it. Samson was buried between Zorah and Eshtaol in his father's tomb.

etam-2.title: Etam
etam-2.note: The rock of Etam, where Samson went down into a cleft and stayed after he had cut down the Philistines.

gaal.title: Gaal
gaal.note: He talked the people of Shechem into rising against Abimelech. When Abimelech brought his forces against the city, Gaal was beaten and driven out.

gaash.title: Gaash
gaash.note: Joshua was buried near this hill in Ephraim, close to Timnath-heres.

gaba-2.title: Gaba
gaba-2.note: Named once, in Judges, and nowhere else.

gaba-4.title: Gaba
gaba-4.note: Judges names him once, and nothing else is recorded.

gazathite.title: Gazathite
gazathite.note: A man of Gaza. Judges uses it for the men who waited at the gate to kill Samson, and he carried the gate off.

gazer.title: Gazer
gazer.note: The same city as Gezer. Pharaoh took it and gave it to his daughter when she married Solomon, and Solomon fortified it along with Hazor and Megiddo. The Gezer Calendar, a little tablet of farming seasons in early Hebrew script, was found there.

gera-2.title: Gera
gera-2.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
gera-2.note: The name ran in the Benjamite tribe. This Gera is in Genesis 46:21 and in 1 Chronicles 8:5, and Judges 3:15 makes a Gera the father of Ehud, the left-handed judge.

gerizim.title: Gerizim
gerizim.note: Opposite Mount Ebal, near Shechem. Six tribes stood on Gerizim to speak the blessings while six on Ebal spoke the curses, as Moses had ordered and Joshua carried out. The Samaritans later built a temple on top as a rival to Jerusalem, which is what the Samaritan woman is asking Jesus about in John 4:20.

gershon.title: Gershon
gershon.about: Levite living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
gershon.note: Levi's eldest son. His descendants carried the tabernacle's coverings, curtains and hangings by cart through the wilderness. Exodus 2:22 and 18:3, filed under this name, belong to a different man.

gideon.title: Gideon
gideon.note: An angel found him threshing wheat in a winepress, hiding it from the Midianites, and called him a mighty man of valour. Gideon asked for the fleece to be wet and then dry before he believed it. God cut his army from thirty-two thousand to three hundred, and they took the Midianite camp at night with torches, trumpets and empty jars.

gidom.title: Gidom
gidom.note: Judges 20:45 names it once, as a point on the road where the retreating Benjamite army was cut down. It lay somewhere between Gibeah and the rock of Rimmon, and nobody knows exactly where.

gilead.title: Gilead
gilead.note: Hill country east of the Jordan, split by the Jabbok between Og in the north and Sihon in the south before the conquest. Gad, Reuben and half of Manasseh got it, and its rough ground made it a refuge for Jacob running from Laban and David running from Absalom. Jeremiah's question about balm in Gilead comes from its trade in balm and spices.

gilead-3.title: Gilead
gilead-3.note: One of 4 men called Gilead. This one is a man from the years before the monarchy, named twice in Judges.

gileadite.title: Gileadite
gileadite.note: Someone from Gilead, east of the Jordan, or of the clan named after Machir's son. Jephthah is the best known, the judge who beat the Ammonites and made the rash vow about his daughter.

gilgal.title: Gilgal
gilgal.note: Israel's first camp after crossing the Jordan. The people were circumcised there and kept their first Passover in the land, and later Samuel judged at Gilgal and Saul was confirmed as king there.

god.title: God
god.note: The Bible never argues that he exists; it assumes it, and Psalm 14:1 calls the man who denies it a fool. The Hebrew is El, from a word meaning strong, or Eloah, far more often in the plural Elohim. Jehovah, the other name, is printed LORD in small capitals in the Authorized Version.

hamath.title: Hamath
hamath.note: An Aramean capital on the Orontes in Upper Syria, the old northern limit of the land promised to Israel. Its king Toi was David's ally. Inscribed stones from the site, set up by a king the Assyrians called Irhuleni, were among the first Hieroglyphic Luwian texts European scholars saw, and reading his name gave them some of the script's first sign values.

hamor.title: Hamor
hamor.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
hamor.note: The Canaanite ruler of Shechem. His son raped Dinah, and while Hamor tried to arrange a marriage, Simeon and Levi talked the men of the city into circumcision and killed them while they were still in pain.

harosheth.title: Harosheth
harosheth.note: Sisera's base, the Canaanite general who led Jabin's iron chariots. Barak broke his army at the Kishon and chased what was left back here. Where exactly it was is still argued over, near Mount Carmel or a district name for several settlements.

hazor.title: Hazor
hazor.note: The head of all the Canaanite kingdoms, in Joshua's words, and the biggest city-state in the region. Its fall decided the northern campaign. The dig there found a huge Bronze Age city to match.

heber-2.title: Heber
heber-2.note: A Kenite, and his wife Jael killed Sisera in her tent when the Canaanite general came running. That fulfilled Deborah's word that a woman would get the credit.

hebron.title: Hebron
hebron.note: Abraham camped near here at Mamre and bought the cave of Machpelah to bury Sarah. It sits in the hill country south of Jerusalem, once called Kirjath-arba, and Joshua gave it to Caleb. David reigned there seven years before moving to Jerusalem, and Herod's great stone enclosure over the traditional tomb still stands.

helbah.title: Helbah
helbah.note: Asher never drove the Canaanites out of this town in the coastal plain of Phoenicia, and it has not been matched to a modern site.

heres.title: Heres
heres.note: Sun. The Amorites held Mount Heres with Aijalon and Shaalbim until the house of Joseph subdued them, and Gideon came back from chasing the Midianite kings by the ascent of Heres. Whether that is one place or two is not certain.

heshbon.title: Heshbon
heshbon.note: Sihon's capital, east of the Jordan near the northern edge of Moab. Moses took it before Israel crossed into Canaan, and it became a Levitical city in Reuben. Moab later had it back, which is why the prophets name it in their judgments on Moab, and the ruins, still called Hesban, lie about twenty miles east of the Jordan.

hillel.title: Hillel
hillel.note: Father of Abdon, the judge who came after Jephthah, and a Pirathonite from the hill country of Ephraim. He has nothing to do with the later rabbi of the same name.

hittite.title: Hittite
hittite.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
hittite.note: Ephron the Hittite sold Abraham the cave of Machpelah at Hebron, and Uriah, the soldier whose wife David took, was a Hittite too. Critics once doubted there was ever a Hittite nation, until digs at Boghazkoy in Turkey found its capital. The Hittites in Canaan were probably a smaller offshoot, or the name used loosely.

hivite.title: Hivite
hivite.note: One of the peoples in the land before Israel. At Shechem a Hivite's son raped Dinah, and at Gibeon Hivites tricked Joshua into a treaty by pretending to come from far off, which put the city under Israel's protection.

hobab.title: Hobab
hobab.about: Midianite living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
hobab.note: Moses asked him to be Israel's guide out of Sinai, since he knew the wilderness. He was a Kenite related to Jethro, and Judges uses a word for him that has led some to think he was Jethro himself. His descendants settled near Jericho and later around Arad.

hormah.title: Hormah
hormah.note: Its name means "devoted to destruction", and it was first called Zephath. Israel was beaten there after going into Canaan without the Lord, following the spies' report. Later Israel vowed to destroy the cities of the region, and the vow, kept under Joshua, gave the town its name.

ibleam.title: Ibleam
ibleam.note: A town given to Manasseh inside Issachar's borders, where the Canaanites were never driven out. King Ahaziah of Judah took his death wound near there, running from Jehu. It is generally identified with Khirbet Bel'ameh, near Jenin.

ibzan.title: Ibzan
ibzan.note: He judged Israel from Bethlehem for seven years and had thirty sons and thirty daughters. Nothing else of his rule is recorded.

ishmaelite.title: Ishmaelite
ishmaelite.about: Abraham's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
ishmaelite.note: The Ishmaelites came from Abraham's son Ishmael and traded across the country south and east of Canaan. One of their caravans bought Joseph from his brothers and took him down to Egypt.

israel.title: Israel
israel.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
israel.note: God gave Jacob this name after he wrestled through the night at Peniel. It became the name of the nation that came from his twelve sons, and later of the northern kingdom and of the land. For the man himself, see Jacob.

issachar.title: Issachar
issachar.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
issachar.note: Jacob's ninth son. His tribe held the fertile Jezreel Valley, and Chronicles says its men understood the times and knew what Israel ought to do.

jabbok.title: Jabbok
jabbok.note: Jacob crossed this stream alone the night before he met Esau, wrestled until daybreak, and came away named Israel and limping. It runs west into the Jordan through a gorge in Gilead, halfway between the Sea of Galilee and the Dead Sea, and is the Zarqa River today.

jabin.title: Jabin
jabin.note: King of Hazor, and master of Sisera, whom Deborah and Barak beat. A Psalm still asks God to deal with Israel's enemies as he dealt with Jabin.

jael.title: Jael
jael.note: Sisera ran from the battle to her tent, since her Kenite family was at peace with his king. She gave him milk, let him fall asleep, and drove a tent peg through his head. Deborah had said a woman would get the credit for his death.

jahaz.title: Jahaz
jahaz.note: Moses beat Sihon, the Amorite king, at Jahaz, on the plateau north of the Arnon. The town went to Reuben and then to the Merarite Levites, and because it changed hands with Moab more than once, Isaiah and Jeremiah both name it in their oracles against Moab.

jair-2.title: Jair
jair-2.note: Judges names him twice, and he is a judge from the years before the monarchy.

jair.title: Jair
jair.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
jair.note: He judged Israel twenty-two years. His thirty sons rode thirty donkeys and held thirty towns, which says money and reach, not battles won.

jebus.title: Jebus
jebus.note: What Jerusalem was called while the Jebusites held it. David took it and made it his capital.

jehoshua.title: Jehoshua
jehoshua.about: Judge living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness and Conquest
jehoshua.note: Joshua, in the longer spelling. Moses's attendant and successor, and one of two from the generation out of Egypt who lived to enter the land. He took Israel over the Jordan, brought down Jericho and divided the land among the tribes. The name means Yahweh saves, the same name Greek renders Jesus.

jephthah.title: Jephthah
jephthah.note: Son of a prostitute, thrown out by his half-brothers, and leading a gang of raiders when Gilead's elders came begging him to fight the Ammonites. He vowed to sacrifice whatever came out of his house first after the victory, and it was his daughter, his only child. Judges tells it without approving the vow or explaining why he kept it.

jerubbaal.title: Jerubbaal
jerubbaal.note: "Let Baal contend." Gideon got the name after he pulled down his father's altar to Baal and nothing happened to him, so the name is a taunt at a god who could not answer.

jerusalem.title: Jerusalem
jerusalem.note: David took it from the Jebusites and made it his capital, and once Solomon's temple stood there it was the centre of Israel's worship for a thousand years. Babylon destroyed it, the exiles rebuilt it, Rome destroyed it again in AD 70. Jesus died and rose just outside its walls, and Revelation ends with a new Jerusalem coming down from heaven.

jether-4.title: Jether
jether-4.note: Judges names him once, and he is a man from the years before the monarchy.

jezreel.title: Jezreel
jezreel.note: A valley and town in northern Israel. Naboth's vineyard was there, the one Ahab and Jezebel stole, and it was there that Jehu wiped out Ahab's whole house. Hosea named one of his children Jezreel to say judgment was coming.

joash-3.title: Joash
joash-3.note: Judges 6 makes him the father whose altar his son tore down. When the town came for the son, he told them to let the god plead his own case.

jobesh-gilead.title: Jobesh
jobesh-gilead.note: Better known as Jabesh-gilead, a town in Gilead east of the Jordan. Its men stayed home from the war against Benjamin and were nearly wiped out for it, and their daughters were handed to Benjamin's survivors as wives. When Nahash the Ammonite besieged it, Saul rescued it. Years later its men took his body down from the walls of Beth-shan and buried it.

jogbehah.title: Jogbehah
jogbehah.note: It was one of the towns Gad built and walled east of the Jordan. Gideon went past it on the caravan route, chasing the Midianite kings Zebah and Zalmunna.

jonathan-9.title: Jonathan
jonathan-9.note: A levite from the years before the monarchy, and Judges is the only book that names him.

jordan.title: Jordan
jordan.note: It runs from the slopes of Mount Hermon through the Sea of Galilee and down the Rift Valley to the Dead Sea, about sixty five miles in a straight line and nearer two hundred as the river winds. Israel crossed it on dry ground under Joshua, Elijah and Elisha each parted it, and John the Baptist baptised Jesus in it.

joseph.title: Joseph
joseph.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
joseph.note: Jacob's eleventh son and Rachel's first. His father's favouritism and his own tactless dreams got him sold into Egypt by his brothers, and there he rose from slave to prisoner to second in the land by reading Pharaoh's dreams of famine. When the famine drove his brothers down for grain, he told them who he was and forgave them.

jotham-2.title: Jotham
jotham-2.note: The youngest son, and the only one who got away when his half-brother murdered the other seventy. He stood on a mountain and told the town a fable about trees choosing a bramble for king, then ran for it. By the end of Judges 9 his curse had come true.

judah.title: Judah
judah.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
judah.note: Leah's fourth son, and the brother who ends up leading. He talked the others into selling Joseph rather than killing him, and later offered himself as a hostage in Benjamin's place. His tribe produced David's royal line and gave its name to the southern kingdom, and Jacob's dying blessing promised the sceptre would not leave him.

kadesh.title: Kadesh
kadesh.note: Kadesh-barnea, Israel's main camp in the wilderness of Zin. Moses sent the twelve spies from there, Miriam died there, and there he struck the rock and lost his way into Canaan. It is usually identified with Ain el-Qudeis or Ain el-Qudeirat, where a fortress of the Israelite period has been dug up.

karkor.title: Karkor
karkor.note: Desert country east of the Jordan, past Succoth and Penuel. Gideon caught the Midianite kings Zebah and Zalmunna there and broke what was left of their army, ending seven years in which Israel had hidden in mountain caves.

kedesh.title: Kedesh
kedesh.note: A city of refuge in Galilee, one of six where someone who had killed by accident could run and be safe. Barak came from there, the commander Deborah called up.

kenath-2.title: Kenath
kenath-2.note: Named once, in Judges, and nowhere else.

kenaz-2.title: Kenaz
kenaz-2.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
kenaz-2.note: Caleb's younger brother, and father of Othniel, Israel's first judge.

kenite.title: Kenite
kenite.note: They were a wandering clan close to Midian, outside the twelve tribes but mostly friendly to Israel. Jethro, Moses' father-in-law, was a Kenite priest, and Jael, Heber the Kenite's wife, killed Sisera.

kirjath.title: Kirjath
kirjath.note: Kirjath-jearim, also called Baalah, a Gibeonite town on the line between Judah and Benjamin. The ark sat there twenty years after the Philistines gave it back, until David brought it up to Jerusalem. The prophet Uriah, whom Jehoiakim had killed, came from there.

kirjath-arba.title: Kirjath-arba
kirjath-arba.note: "Arba's city," Hebron's older name, after a great man among the Anakim. Sarah died there and Abraham bought the cave of Machpelah close by to bury her. Joshua gave it to Caleb for the faithful report he brought back as a spy.

kirjath-sannah.title: Kirjath-sannah
kirjath-sannah.note: Another name for Debir, also called Kirjath-sepher, a royal Canaanite city in the hills southwest of Hebron. Caleb promised his daughter Achsah to whoever took it, and his nephew Othniel did.

kishon.title: Kishon
kishon.note: It is a winter stream that drains the Jezreel Valley into the Mediterranean below Mount Carmel, and it floods fast. It swept away Sisera's chariots when Deborah and Barak fought the Canaanites, and in its valley Elijah had the prophets of Baal killed after the contest on Carmel.

kitron.title: Kitron
kitron.note: Zebulun never drove out the Canaanites of this town, so they stayed on as forced labour, and Joshua 19:15 probably lists it as Kattath.

laish.title: Laish
laish.note: Peaceful, cut off, and Canaanite. The tribe of Dan, having failed to settle the land it was given, took the city and renamed it Dan.

lappidoth.title: Lappidoth
lappidoth.note: Deborah's husband, and Scripture says nothing more about him. The name means "torches", and some older readers took it as a word about Deborah herself. The plain reading makes it his name.

lebanon.title: Lebanon
lebanon.note: Two mountain ridges along the coast, Lebanon proper to the west and the Anti-Lebanon rising to Mount Hermon, with the Beqaa Valley between. Solomon's temple and palace were built of its cedar, cut and floated south under a deal with Hiram of Tyre. Israel was promised it and never took all of it.

lebonah.title: Lebonah
lebonah.note: Judges 21:19 uses it to say where Shiloh was, on the road between Bethel and Shechem, when the men of Benjamin grabbed wives from the girls dancing at the festival. It is generally identified with Lubban, south of Nablus, which still keeps the name.

lehi.title: Lehi
lehi.note: "Jawbone." The Philistines gathered here to take Samson, and he broke his ropes and killed a thousand of them with a donkey's jawbone. Afterwards, parched, he called on God, and a spring opened in a hollow there.

luz-2.title: Luz
luz-2.note: Named once, in Judges, and nowhere else.

luz.title: Luz
luz.note: It was the old Canaanite name of Bethel, where Jacob dreamed of the stairway to heaven, and it hung on in a nearby town after Bethel was renamed.

machir.title: Machir
machir.about: Manasseh's son living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
machir.note: Manasseh's son. His clan, the Machirites, were such fighters that Machir's name can stand for the whole half-tribe of Manasseh east of the Jordan.

mahaneh-dan.title: Mahaneh-dan
mahaneh-dan.note: The camp of Dan, behind Kirjath-jearim. Samson first felt the Spirit stirring him here, and later six hundred armed Danites camped on the same ground on their way north to take Laish.

manasseh.title: Manasseh
manasseh.about: Joseph's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
manasseh.note: Joseph's elder son, whom Jacob took as his own and blessed. His name went to one of Israel's twelve tribes, and from Numbers through Joshua and Chronicles most of his verses are about that tribe and its land.

manoah.title: Manoah
manoah.about: Samson's father living before Israel's Monarchy
manoah.note: Samson's father. An angel came to him and his wife, who had no children, to say a son was coming who would be a Nazirite from birth, and when Manoah realised who he had seen he was sure they would both die.

maon.title: Maon
maon.note: About seven miles south of Hebron, in the Judean hill country. David hid from Saul in the wilderness named after it, and Nabal, whose widow Abigail married David, kept his flocks there. The ruins, now Tell Ma'in, still mark the spot.

megiddo.title: Megiddo
megiddo.note: It guarded the pass into the Jezreel Valley. A Canaanite royal city, it went to Manasseh and Solomon rebuilt it as a chariot city. Deborah and Barak beat Sisera on its plain, and King Josiah died there facing Pharaoh Necho, a death mourned so deeply it became proverbial. Thutmose III's siege of it around 1457 BC is carved in detail on the walls of Karnak.

meroz.title: Meroz
meroz.note: The Song of Deborah curses it. The angel of the Lord calls down a curse on Meroz for not coming to help against Sisera's army, while other tribes in the poem are praised for answering. Nobody knows where it was, though some think it sat close to the battle in the Jezreel Valley, which would make staying home worse.

micah.title: Micah
micah.note: In Judges, an Israelite who set up his own shrine with an idol and hired a wandering Levite as his private priest. Most of his verses belong to that story.

midian.title: Midian
midian.note: A people descended from Abraham through Keturah, and they keep turning up in different roles. Midianite traders bought Joseph. Moses found a home and a wife, Zipporah, in Midian. Later they oppressed Israel until Gideon beat them.

minnith.title: Minnith
minnith.note: Jephthah's victory over the Ammonites ran as far as this town. Ezekiel lists wheat from Minnith among the goods Judah sold to Tyre. It stood on the tableland east of the Jordan, somewhere near Heshbon and Rabbah.

mizpeh.title: Mizpeh
mizpeh.note: Another spelling of Mizpah, the watchpost name given to several places in Israel.

moab.title: Moab
moab.note: East of the Dead Sea, the nation descended from Lot through his elder daughter. Israel and Moab went back and forth between enemies and kin: Balak hired Balaam to curse Israel, and yet Ruth, a Moabite, became King David's great-grandmother. King Mesha's own inscription on the Moabite Stone records the wars with Israel that 2 Kings describes.

moreh-2.title: Moreh
moreh-2.note: Named once, in Judges, and nowhere else.

moses.title: Moses
moses.about: Levite living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
moses.note: Born a Hebrew slave in Egypt and raised in Pharaoh's house, he killed an Egyptian overseer and ran to Midian, where he kept sheep for forty years. God called him back from the burning bush to face Pharaoh and lead Israel out. He gave them the law at Sinai, led them forty years in the wilderness, and died at a hundred and twenty within sight of the promised land.

nahalal.title: Nahalal
nahalal.note: A town in Zebulun, later given with its pastures to the Merarite Levites. Zebulun never drove out the Canaanites there and put them to forced labour instead. It is sometimes linked with Tell en-Nahl near the Kishon River.

naphtali.title: Naphtali
naphtali.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
naphtali.note: Jacob's sixth son, born to Rachel's servant Bilhah. His tribe settled in northern Galilee, the land Isaiah says will see a great light, and Matthew ties that to Jesus starting his work there.

non.title: Non
non.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
non.note: Joshua's father, of the tribe of Ephraim, more usually spelled Nun and hardly ever seen outside the phrase "Joshua son of Nun."

ophrah.title: Ophrah
ophrah.note: Gideon's hometown. The angel of the Lord first appeared to him there, and later he set up a golden ephod in the same place, which Israel ended up worshipping.

oreb.title: Oreb
oreb.note: He was one of two Midianite commanders the men of Ephraim killed during Gideon's rout, and the rock where he died took his name.

othniel.title: Othniel
othniel.note: Caleb's younger relative, who won Caleb's daughter Achsah by taking a Canaanite city. He became Israel's first judge and broke eight years of oppression under a Mesopotamian king.

peniel.title: Peniel
peniel.note: Jacob wrestled here through the night by the Jabbok River. He came away with a new name, Israel, and a limp he kept. He called the place Peniel, face of God, because he had seen God face to face and lived.

perizzite.title: Perizzite
perizzite.note: They come almost every time in a list, paired with the Canaanites, as one of the peoples living in Canaan before Israel arrived.

philistine.title: Philistine
philistine.about: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs
philistine.note: Seafaring people who settled the coastal plain between Gezer and Gaza, most likely from Caphtor, which the Old Testament elsewhere identifies as Crete.

phinehas.title: Phinehas
phinehas.about: High Priest living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
phinehas.note: Aaron's grandson, Eleazar's son. When Israel was being struck by a plague for idolatry and sexual sin with Moabite women, Phinehas drove a spear through an Israelite man and a Midianite woman together, and the plague stopped.

phurah.title: Phurah
phurah.note: He was Gideon's servant, likely his armour-bearer. The night before the attack with three hundred men, Gideon took Phurah down to spy on the Midianite camp.

phuvah-2.title: Phuvah
phuvah-2.note: Judges names him once, and he is a man from the years before the monarchy.

pirathon.title: Pirathon
pirathon.note: It was Abdon the judge's town, in the hill country of Ephraim, and he was buried there. Benaiah the Pirathonite, one of David's thirty, also came from it.

pirathonite.title: Pirathonite
pirathonite.note: Two men carry the label, both from Pirathon in Ephraim. Abdon son of Hillel judged Israel for eight years and is remembered for his many sons and grandsons. Benaiah was one of David's thirty.

ramah.title: Ramah
ramah.note: Samuel's hometown, and where he was buried. The name was common enough that several towns carried it. Jeremiah's Rachel weeping for her children is set here too.

ramath-lehi.title: Ramath-lehi
ramath-lehi.note: "Height of the jawbone." Samson named it after he killed a thousand Philistines there with a donkey's jawbone. It lay somewhere in the Shephelah.

rehob.title: Rehob
rehob.note: The far edge of the spies' route into Canaan, up in the north. Asher was allotted a Rehob too, and Judges 1:31 says Asher never drove out the people living there.

remmon-2.title: Remmon
remmon-2.note: In Judges 20 the last six hundred survivors of the tribe ran to the rock of Rimmon and held out there for four months. Later the other tribes sent word to them there and made peace.

reuben.title: Reuben
reuben.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
reuben.note: Jacob's firstborn. He slept with one of his father's concubines and lost the birthright for it, and Jacob had not forgotten it on his deathbed.

samson.title: Samson
samson.note: He was set apart before birth as a Nazirite, with the rule that his hair was never to be cut, and his strength held as long as the vow did, enough to kill a lion with his bare hands and Philistines by the score.

seir.title: Seir
seir.note: A rough range of mountains east of the Arabah. It runs from the bottom of the Dead Sea toward the Gulf of Aqabah. The Horites lived there first, and Esau's descendants pushed them out.

seirath.title: Seirath
seirath.note: Ehud ran here after he killed Eglon, the Moabite king, and rallied Israel before going back down to attack. It was in the hill country of Ephraim, near the border of Benjamin.

shaalabbin.title: Shaalabbin
shaalabbin.note: Allotted to Dan, but the Danites never fully took it, and Amorites held on there until they were put to forced labour. It is also spelled Shaalbim.

shamgar.title: Shamgar
shamgar.note: Son of Anath. He saved Israel from the Philistines by killing six hundred men with an ox goad, the long pointed pole used to drive cattle, and the Song of Deborah remembers him.

shamir.title: Shamir
shamir.note: Tola, the judge, lived at Shamir in the hill country of Ephraim, and Judges 10:1 and 10:2 name it as his home.

shechem.title: Shechem
shechem.note: Abram stopped here when he first came into the land, and Joseph's brothers were grazing the flocks near it when Joseph went looking for them. The city took its name from a Canaanite prince.

sheshai.title: Sheshai
sheshai.about: Man living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
sheshai.note: One of the sons of Anak. Caleb drove him out of Hebron when he finally claimed the land promised to him decades earlier.

shiloh.title: Shiloh
shiloh.note: The tabernacle stood at Shiloh, north of Bethel in Ephraim, for most of the time of the judges. Young Samuel served there. After the Philistines captured the ark, the place faded.

sibboleth.title: Sibboleth
sibboleth.note: How the men of Ephraim said shibboleth, because their dialect had no sh sound. Jephthah's men used the word at the fords. It picked them out and got them killed.

sidon.title: Sidon
sidon.note: The older of the two great Phoenician ports, north of Tyre. It was allotted to Asher, but Asher never took it.

sihon.title: Sihon
sihon.about: King living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
sihon.note: An Amorite king. Israel asked to pass through his land, and he attacked them instead. It cost him his kingdom east of the Jordan.

simeon.title: Simeon
simeon.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
simeon.note: Jacob's second son. With his brother Levi he killed the men of Shechem after their sister Dinah was raped. Jacob held it against them on his deathbed.

sinai.title: Sinai
sinai.note: Also called Horeb. Israel camped at the foot of the mountain for about a year after the exodus, and the law came down through Moses here.

sisera.title: Sisera
sisera.about: Deborah's adversary living before Israel's Monarchy
sisera.note: He commanded the Canaanite army that held Israel down for twenty years, until Deborah and Barak beat it. Sisera ran on foot to the tent of a woman called Jael, who took him in and then killed him.

sorek.title: Sorek
sorek.note: Delilah lived in the Valley of Sorek, and the Philistine lords paid her there to find out where Samson's strength came from.

succoth.title: Succoth
succoth.note: Jacob built shelters for his cattle here, east of the Jordan near the Jabbok, on his way back from Paddan-aram. The name means booths.

taanach.title: Taanach
taanach.note: A Canaanite royal city on the southwest edge of the Jezreel Valley, near Megiddo. Joshua beat its king, the town went to the Levites of Kohath, and its Canaanites were never driven out. Deborah's song puts a battle there by the waters of Megiddo.

tabbath.title: Tabbath
tabbath.note: When Gideon's three hundred broke the Midianite camp, the army ran toward Tabbath, near the Jordan south of Beth-shean.

tabor.title: Tabor
tabor.note: A dome-shaped mountain rising out of the Jezreel Valley, on the line between Zebulun and Issachar. Deborah sent Barak there to gather Israel before the battle with Sisera. The psalmist sets it beside Hermon, and Hosea and Jeremiah both name it in oracles of judgment.

talmai-2.title: Talmai
talmai-2.about: King living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
talmai-2.note: Caleb drove three Anakim giants out of Hebron, and Talmai was one of them.

thebez.title: Thebez
thebez.note: Abimelech, Gideon's son who made himself king, was besieging the tower at Thebez when a woman dropped a millstone on his head. He told his armor-bearer to kill him so nobody could say a woman did it. Joab still remembered it years later.

timnah.title: Timnah
timnah.note: The Philistine town where Samson saw the woman he wanted to marry. The riddle at that wedding feast started his long fight with the Philistines.

timnath-heres.title: Timnath-heres
timnath-heres.note: The name means portion of the sun. Joshua was given this town in the hill country of Ephraim and was buried there, north of the hill of Gaash. The book of Joshua spells it Timnath-serah.

timnite.title: Timnite
timnite.note: Samson's Philistine father-in-law, a man of Timnah. When his daughter was given to another man, the trouble that followed ended with his household burned.

tob.title: Tob
tob.note: Jephthah's half-brothers drove him out for being a prostitute's son, and he went to the land of Tob, east of Gilead. He gathered outlaws there until Gilead's elders came to fetch him back to fight the Ammonites. Men of Tob later hired themselves out to the Ammonites.

tola-2.title: Tola
tola-2.note: Judges names him once, and he is a judge from the years before the monarchy.

zaannannim.title: Zaannannim
zaannannim.note: On Naphtali's border, near Kedesh, by the oak where Heber the Kenite had his tent. Sisera ran there after his army broke at the Kishon, and Heber's wife Jael killed him.

zalmon.title: Zalmon
zalmon.about: Warrior living at the time of United Monarchy
zalmon.note: Two things. A wooded hill near Shechem, where Abimelech's men cut brushwood to burn the tower of Shechem, and Psalm 68 has snow on it. And Zalmon the Ahohite, one of David's mighty men.

zalmunna.title: Zalmunna
zalmunna.note: He and Zebah were the Midianite kings who had killed Gideon's brothers. Gideon chased them down and caught them, told his young son to kill them, and when the boy was too frightened, did it himself.

zareah.title: Zareah
zareah.note: Samson's hometown, better known as Zorah, on the border of Judah and Dan. The angel of the Lord told Manoah's wife there that she would have a son, and Samson was buried between Zorah and Eshtaol.

zebah.title: Zebah
zebah.note: Gideon's other Midianite king, caught with Zalmunna. Both had killed his brothers, and he executed them himself.

zebul.title: Zebul
zebul.note: He ran Shechem for Abimelech. When Gaal stirred the city up, Zebul sent word to Abimelech, and he helped put the revolt down while the city around him turned.

zebulonite.title: Zebulonite
zebulonite.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
zebulonite.note: Someone of the tribe of Zebulun. In Judges it is Elon, who judged Israel ten years and was buried at Aijalon in Zebulun's land.

zebulun.title: Zebulun
zebulun.about: Jacob's son living at the time of the Patriarchs
zebulun.note: Jacob's tenth son and Leah's last. His tribe's land ran up to the Sea of Galilee, and Isaiah names it with Naphtali as the place where a light would dawn, which Matthew applies to Jesus in Galilee.

zeeb.title: Zeeb
zeeb.note: They named a winepress after him, because that is where the men of Ephraim killed him. He was one of two Midianite commanders caught in Gideon's rout.

zephath.title: Zephath
zephath.note: Judah and Simeon took this Canaanite town, destroyed it, and renamed it Hormah. It had beaten back an Israelite attack years earlier in the wilderness. After that the old name drops out.

zererath.title: Zererath
zererath.note: The Midianites ran toward it when Gideon routed them, down the Jordan valley toward Beth-shittah and Abel-meholah, and the site is unknown.

zippor.title: Zippor
zippor.about: Moabite living at the time of Egypt and Wilderness
zippor.note: Balak's father. Balak was the Moabite king who hired Balaam to curse Israel.
